title: Why Do People Need Insurance? 5 Realities That Protect Your Future
description: Explore the 5 non-negotiable reasons individuals and families require insurance: bankruptcy shielding, statutory compliance, mortgage mandates, and intergenerational stability.
author: Marcus Vance

content.text: Insurance is not about preparing for everyday minor inconveniences; it is about shielding your household from financially fatal events. In personal finance, offensive strategies build wealth, but insurance is the foundational defense that prevents that wealth from being eradicated.
The 5 Reasons Insurance Is Mandatory for Financial Survival

items: Bankruptcy Prevention: Medical catastrophes and major liability lawsuits remain leading drivers of personal bankruptcies according to the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/).
Statutory & Legal Requirements: Driving without auto liability insurance is illegal across 49 US states and throughout the UK and EU, carrying heavy fines, license suspension, or vehicle impoundment.
Securing Credit and Mortgages: Banks will not issue a 30-year home loan without documented proof of hazard insurance protecting their collateral.

Preserving Family Standard of Living: If the primary earner dies, a [term life policy](/learn/term-insurance-guide) ensures surviving children can remain in their home and attend university without financial panic.

Capping Maximum Loss Exposure: A policy with an [out-of-pocket maximum](/glossary/out-of-pocket-maximum) guarantees that even a $1,000,000 cancer treatment will not cost your family more than your contractually agreed ceiling.

content.title: The Self-Insurance Fallacy
content.text: Some consumers attempt to 'self-insure' by keeping $20,000 in a savings account. While this covers minor car dents or appliance repairs, it is hopelessly inadequate for a $2,000,000 auto accident liability judgment or a $600,000 house rebuilding cost after a wildfire.
Core Protections Ranked by Financial Priority

rows: Hundreds of thousands in intensive care, surgery, and prescription bills.
Multi-million dollar bodily injury judgments if you cause a multi-vehicle crash.
Complete structural loss and personal property replacement following fire.
Decades of lost income replacement for surviving spouse and children.
Loss of your most valuable wealth-building asset: your ability to earn a living.

content.title: Quantify Your Family's Protection Need
content.description: Determine the exact capital cushion required to retire your mortgage and secure your dependents.

items.question: Do single people with no children need life insurance?
items.answer: Usually no, unless they carry co-signed private student loans or debts that would burden their surviving parents. However, single individuals urgently need health and disability insurance.

content.text: Individual risk profiles depend on net worth, debt structure, and local statutory requirements. Always evaluate your portfolio holistically.
